title: Ride-on sweeper for car parks, courtyards and entrances
audience: Trained and authorised operators of a ride-on sweeper, and the supervisors who assign them work on car parks, courtyards, entrances and similar outdoor hard surfaces.
learningOutcomes: Complete a pre-operation check and review the manufacturer's manual before using a ride-on sweeper.
Operate the sweeper's controls in the correct order, and shut it down safely at the end of a run.
Name the noise, heat, debris and exhaust hazards this machine presents, and apply a control to each.

instruction.heading: Who may operate, and what the operator must know
instruction.body: Only a trained and authorised person may operate a ride-on sweeper. Before the first use, the operator reads the manufacturer's manual, knows where every control and attachment is and what it does, and works under supervision until the supervisor is satisfied. Passengers are never carried on the machine. This lesson does not give anyone authority to operate plant.

instruction.heading: Hazards on the machine
instruction.body: The rotating brush can throw debris into the air and into the eyes of the operator or a bystander. The hydraulic drive, the motor and the exhaust can become hot during operation, so they must not be touched while running or soon after. Exhaust fumes can make an operator dizzy or queasy, so the sweeper is not run where fumes can collect. Noise over a shift can harm hearing, and vibration adds to body strain. Smoking and open flames are not allowed near the machine, and the operator avoids repeated stooping and twisting when clearing it.

instruction.heading: Starting, moving and stopping
instruction.body: Open the suction flap, start the sweeping and side brushes, free the parking brake, and press the accelerator gently to the speed the job needs. To slow down, lift off to neutral and then apply the service brake. Engage the parking brake when you stop. Never lift the hopper while the centre broom is still turning; halt the broom first, then operate the hopper.

instruction.heading: Clearing the route before you sweep
instruction.body: Lift out big items by hand and place them in the waste container before the sweeper passes over the area. Large objects can jam the brush or damage the machine. Check the route for pedestrians and vehicles, and set signs and cones so people know the sweeper is working.

instruction.heading: Shutdown, filter and storage
instruction.body: When the run ends, switch off the roller and the side brush, engage the parking brake, and check and clean the filter as the manufacturer directs. Empty the debris bin when it is full or at the end of the shift. Wash down the machine and park it in its assigned storage area. Never walk away from the unit while the engine is still running.

procedure: Put on the PPE the task requires, including eye protection, hearing protection and suitable footwear.
Carry out the pre-operation check: manual to hand, controls, brakes, brushes, hopper, filter, lights, and any damage or inspection tag.
Lift big items out by hand and drop them into the waste container.
Set signs and cones for pedestrians and vehicles on the route.
Open the suction flap, start the sweeping and side brushes, and free the parking brake.
Ease up to the working speed the job needs. Reduce speed by applying the service brake, not by stopping abruptly.
Sweep the route. Keep the hopper down while the centre broom turns.
At the end of the run, switch the brushes off, engage the parking brake, check and clean the filter, and empty the debris bin.
Wash down the machine, park it in storage, take off the PPE and wash your hands.

workedExamples.situation: A plastic bag catches under the sweeper's brush shortly after you start in a courtyard.
workedExamples.reasoning: Switch off the brushes and set the parking brake before you touch anything. Do not reach under the running machine. Once it is stopped and the parking brake is on, remove the bag by hand, then check the brush and bearings for damage before you restart.

workedExamples.situation: A colleague asks for a ride to the far end of the car park on the sweeper, to save a walk.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Passengers are not carried on the machine. Walk the colleague to the far end, or use a different vehicle, and then continue the sweep yourself.

equipmentAndPpe: Ride-on sweeper, operated only by an authorised person
Signs and cones for the route
Gloves and footwear suited to outdoor work

commonErrors.error: Climbing down while the motor still runs.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop the engine and set the parking brake before leaving the seat.

commonErrors.error: Touching the motor or a hydraulic line straight after running.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat these parts as hot until they have cooled, and wait for the machine to cool before servicing it.

commonErrors.error: Raising the hopper while the centre broom is turning.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop the centre broom first, then operate the hopper.

commonErrors.error: Sweeping without ear and eye protection.
commonErrors.prevention: Put on eye and hearing protection before the machine is started.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not grant authority to operate plant. Check the local requirement and the manufacturer's manual before any operator is assigned.
Exhaust fumes can make people dizzy or queasy.
Noise, vibration and sun exposure are hazards in the reference document.

qualityStandard: A pre-operation check is recorded before each use.
The route is cleared of large objects and signed before sweeping starts.
The machine is shut down, with the parking brake set and the engine off, before it is left.
The debris bin is emptied and the filter checked at the end of each run.
documentationEvidence: Operator authorisation record, as the business sets it
Defect report for any fault or damage found
summary: Only trained and authorised operators run the machine, and no passengers are carried.
Clear large objects, sign the route, and set the brakes before leaving the machine.
Hot, rotating and noisy parts need protection and respect at all times.

knowledgeChecks.question: Who may operate a ride-on sweeper?
options: Anyone who has watched it run once and feels confident enough to use it on any site.
Only trained and authorised operators, after reading the manual and working under supervision.
Any cleaner, provided a trained passenger is on board and the passenger is willing to supervise

knowledgeChecks.question: A plastic bag catches in the brush while the sweeper is running. What comes first?
options: Reach under the machine and pull the bag free while the brushes are still turning
Switch off the brushes and set the parking brake before touching anything.
Keep moving until the bag comes free on its own, without stopping.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the correct approach to raising the dust hopper?
options: Raise it while the centre broom turns to clear dust.
Stop the centre broom first, then operate the hopper.
Raise it straight away, because the guard blocks contact.
